ideas: Who the teacher was and what they taught
Their teaching style and a memorable lesson
How your thinking changed because of them

phrases.meaning: question what people believe is true
make a subject interesting and real
encourage someone strongly to do something

phrases.phrase: there's no such thing as a stupid question

phrases.meaning: see things from a new angle

model: The teacher who changed how I think was Mr Hoang, who taught me literature in my last two years of high school. Before his class, I used to believe there was always one correct answer. In most subjects we would memorise model essays and repeat them in exams, and I was quite good at that. But Mr Hoang refused to give us model answers. Instead, he would ask us really open questions, like whether a character in a novel was a hero or a coward, and then he'd push us to argue both sides. At first I hated it, because I didn't know what he wanted. But he always said there's no such thing as a stupid question, so slowly I started to speak up. He also brought the subject to life by connecting old stories to things happening in the news. I remember one lesson where we compared a classic poem with a pop song, and it completely opened my eyes to how similar they were. More than anything, he taught me to think for myself and challenge assumptions, including my own. I no longer accept things just because an expert or a textbook says so, and I try to look at things differently before making up my mind. He definitely left a mark on me, and I still use that way of thinking at work today.
